cases.head: 009f41901ee1a943ce85425652bc454fe85d2278
cases.title: Fix .Update() marking AfterSaveBehavior.Throw properties as modified via DetectChanges
cases.body:
Fixes #38105

`DbContext.Update()` on an entity with a nullable complex type + discriminator throws during `SaveChanges`:

```
InvalidOperationException: The property 'X.Discriminator' is defined as read-only
after it has been saved, but its value has been modified or marked as modified.
```

Regression from #37394: the snapshot factory stores default values for shadow properties on complex types, so `DetectChanges` finds a false mismatch between the current discriminator value (set by value generator) and the snapshot (null), re-marking the `Throw` property as modified after `SetEntityState` correctly unflagged it.

### Changes

- **`InternalEntryBase.SetEntityState`**: In the `modifyProperties` block, after unflagging `Throw` properties, set their original values to match current values (guarded by `!IsConceptualNull(property)`) inline in the same loop so `DetectChanges` won't find a false mismatch and re-mark them as modified.

- **Test**: Added `Update_entity_with_nullable_complex_type_and_discriminator_does_not_throw` — inserts entity with nullable complex type + discriminator, clears tracker, calls `Update()` with a new disconnected instance, asserts `SaveChangesAsync` succeeds.

A more targeted fix is proposed in #38111, but I believe this is a more robust approach

cases.title: Issue #18 - adding word-based statistics
cases.body:
This PR addresses issue #18 by adding word-based statistics, very similar to what was done with phrases. A list of the top 25 most-frequently-occurring words is gathered when statistics are loaded. Short words (currently defined as having fewer than 5 characters) are excluded from the search, because they are not interesting. The top 25 results are displayed on a new "Most common words" tab in the `StatisticsDialog`. The user is also offered a simple search form, where on-the-fly searching for specific words is possible. The minimum word length is ignored when searching for specific words.

Additionally, a count of globally unique words (including short words) is calculated during statistics loading. This is also displayed on the Words tab. Code was added to allow this feature to be disabled easily later, but currently it is always enabled.

Closes #18

## Summary
Extends the chart `Legend` with optional **label**, **size** (`sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`), and **orientation** (`horizontal` | `vertical`). The root now wraps the list in a column layout with `display: inline-flex`, scales label text and swatches via CSS using `data-size`, and **extends `FlexProps`** so consumers (and built-in charts) can control alignment—e.g. `alignSelf="center"` to keep legends centered when the default is no longer `justify-content: center` on the list.
## Why
- Support vertical stacking of legend items when horizontal space is tight.
- Support typography/swatch scaling for different chart densities.
- Optional visible heading that doubles as the list’s accessible name when `label` is set; otherwise behavior falls back to `aria-label="Chart legend"`.
- Charts need explicit centering after the legend’s internal layout change.
## Changes
- **`Legend` API**: `label?`, `size?` (default `md`), `orientation?` (default `horizontal`); inherits omitted `FlexProps<'div'>` (minus `children`) for the root.
- **Structure**: Outer root `Flex` + optional label + inner `role="list"` with row/column direction and spacing tuned per orientation.
- **Styles**: `.root`, `.label`, size variants on `data-size`, swatch dimensions tied to legend font size tokens.
- **Bar chart / line chart**: Pass `alignSelf="center"` for top/bottom legends so placement matches prior centered appearance.
- **Design tokens**: `@property --_fs-base` syntax updated from `<length>` to `*` in `variables.css` (broader compatibility with token usage).
- **Docs & Storybook**: README sections and stories for With label, Vertical, and size chart; new example files.
- **Tests**: Snapshot updates for legend and charts; new node snapshots for label, vertical, and sizes; browser tests for label a11y name and vertical list items.

Mirrors the existing `ADDITIONAL_REPOS` (GitHub) pattern for Hugging Face. Each entry specifies the repo ID and its type since HF API endpoints differ by repo type.

### Config format

```yaml
ADDITIONAL_HF_REPOS:
  - repo: "user/dataset-name"
    type: "datasets"
  - repo: "user/model-name"
    type: "models"
  - repo: "user/space-name"

Added config validation and module-scope variable.
- **`scripts/export-tags.js`**: Same fetch-and-merge logic so the tag export script picks up tags from additional HF repos.
- **`public/config.yaml`**: New parameter with commented usage examples.
- **`README.md`**: Documented `ADDITIONAL_HF_REPOS` alongside `ADDITIONAL_REPOS`.

cases.title: Fix incomplete CRUD, stale form state, and missing delete-activity test from PR #8
cases.body:
PR #8 implemented `useInventory` with full CRUD including `updateItem`, but the hook's Update path was never wired to the UI, the Add modal leaked form state across open/close cycles, and the delete activity side-effect had no test coverage.

## Changes

- **Complete the Update path (`updateItem`)**
  - `AddItemModal` gains optional `editItem` / `onUpdate` props; toggles title and submit label between *Add New Item* / *Edit Item* modes
  - `InventoryTable` adds a per-row **Edit** button (cyan, beside Delete)
  - `InventoryPage` manages `editingItem` state and a unified `openModal(item?)` helper
  - `App.tsx` now destructures and passes `updateItem` down to `InventoryPage`

- **Form reset on modal close**  
  A `modalKey` counter in `InventoryPage` increments on every `openModal()` call, forcing React to remount `AddItemModal` fresh — no residual state from a cancelled session. Edit mode pre-fills via a `useState` function initializer.

  ```tsx
  // InventoryPage.tsx
  const openModal = (item?: InventoryItem) => {
    setEditingItem(item)
    setModalKey(prev => prev + 1)   // force remount → clean form
    setIsModalOpen(true)
  }

  <AddItemModal key={modalKey} editItem={editingItem} onUpdate={onUpdate} ... />
  ```

- **Missing test: delete creates activity**  
  Added `'adds activity when deleting an item'` to `useInventory.test.ts`; asserts `activities` grows by 1 with `action: 'removed'` and the correct `itemName`.

cases.head: bc2ac1a4be2e0583597f65d48321802736e3d1a6
cases.title: test: extract ComponentTestBase and remove real-time residue
cases.body:
## Summary

Extract shared test helpers into `ComponentTestBase` and eliminate real-time residue (`CountDownLatch`, `Dispatchers.Default` polling) from all 5 component test classes. Closes #23, relates to wspulse/.github#22.

## Changes

- Add `ComponentTestBase` abstract class with `testScheduler`, `testClient`, `tearDown()`, `clientConfig()`, `waitUntil()` (scheduler-driven, no real delays), and `waitForPing()`.
- Migrate `BasicTest`, `CallbackTest`, `LifecycleTest`, `MiscTest`, `ReconnectTest` to extend `ComponentTestBase(TestCoroutineScheduler())`.
- Replace all `CountDownLatch` usage with `CompletableDeferred<Unit>`.
- Replace all FQN `kotlinx.coroutines.test.runTest` with `runTest(StandardTestDispatcher(testScheduler))` to share the scheduler between base class and test scope.
- Remove duplicated `testClient` fields, `@AfterEach tearDown()` methods, and private helper functions from all 5 test classes.
- Remove unused imports from migrated files.
- Net diff: +154 / -339 lines (185 lines removed).

## Residual time-related patterns (all safe, non-flaky)

After the migration, a small number of time-related patterns remain. Each is bounded and will not cause flakiness:

| Pattern | Location | Why safe |
|---|---|---|
| `runBlocking` | `ComponentTestBase.tearDown()` | `@AfterEach` cannot be `suspend`; this is the required JUnit5 boundary. The client is already closed by the time teardown runs, so `done.await()` completes immediately. |
| `CompletableDeferred.await()` | All test bodies | Suspends, does not block a thread. The client uses `UnconfinedTestDispatcher`, which dispatches callbacks synchronously in the same call stack as `injectClose()` / `injectError()`. The deferred is always completed before `await()` is reached. |
| `withTimeout(1.seconds)` | `ReconnectTest` — close during reconnect | Runs inside `runTest`, so `1.seconds` is virtual time, not wall time. `transportDropSignal` is completed synchronously by `UnconfinedTestDispatcher` before the timeout fires. |
| `delay(60.seconds)` | `ReconnectTest` — slow dialer stub | Runs inside a coroutine on `UnconfinedTestDispatcher`. `client.close()` cancels it before the delay elapses; the test advances only 5 ms of virtual time. The 60-second delay is never actually waited on. |

## Checklist

### Required

- [x] `make check` passes (lint -> test)
- [x] Each commit represents exactly one logical change
- [x] Commit messages follow the format in `commit-message-instructions.md`
- [x] No unrelated code reformatting in this PR

cases.head: b6e16d4e6d0553bc5b1d9634248cb11ad27bdd7b
cases.title: Add NSIP enrichment report for lambing record — FLE082 × NCS310
cases.body:
Lambing record issue #26 for a first-time yearling dam (6401492025FLE082) and genotyped sire (6402382024NCS310), single lamb born 2026-04-14 unassisted, required NSIP enrichment per the breeding record workflow.

## Report: `reports/2026-04-15-lambing-event/report.md`

- **Dam (FLE082)**: Beyond Blessed Farm yearling ewe (born Feb 2025, first lambing); strong growth EBVs — PWWT 72nd pct, YWT 71st pct; NLB 45% accuracy, will build with progeny data
- **Sire (NCS310)**: NC State University 50K-genotyped ram (born Feb 2024); standout BWT EBV of **-0.225 lbs at 80% accuracy** — well-suited for yearling dams; 25 existing progeny
- **Inbreeding**: 🟢 0% COI — clean outcross between VA farm and NC university genetics; no shared ancestors at any generation
- **Predicted offspring**: BWT +0.06 lbs (below breed midpoint +0.18) due to sire's negative BWT offsetting dam's slightly elevated figure; PWWT and YWT well above breed midpoint from dam's genetics
- **Breed context**: Full Katahdin trait ranges with percentile positions for both parents across BWT, WWT, PWWT, YWT, NLB
- **Pedigree**: Two-generation lineage for both parents; USDA-ARS Booneville and Hound River Farm ancestry in dam line; VPI and Hound River (NWT012, SRC: 134.96) in sire line

cases.head: 8be727e43f0bfd1dd285794ce5c557b5ea44336e
cases.title: Size and lay out class diagram nodes from compartment content
cases.body:
Class diagram nodes were sized only from their primary label, causing compartment text (attributes, methods, stereotypes) to clip or overflow the rendered box.

## Layout engine (`DefaultLayoutEngine.cs`)

- Added `SizeClassNode`: width = widest content across class name, annotations, and all compartment lines + 2×padding; height = header section + per-compartment sections (divider + compact padding + lines)
- `SizeStandardNode` delegates to `SizeClassNode` when `node.Compartments.Count > 0`; all non-compartment nodes are unaffected
- Stores `label:centerY` (class name center within header, not full-node center) and `class:headerHeight` in `Node.Metadata` for renderer use
- Directional BFS layer layout is fully preserved — no new graph algorithm introduced

## Renderer (`SvgNodeWriter.cs`)

- Added `AppendClassCompartments`, called from `AppendNode` when compartments or annotations are present
- Renders annotations centered above the class name in the header
- Draws full-width `<line>` dividers at `class:headerHeight` and between compartments using `baseStroke`/`theme.StrokeWidth`
- Renders compartment lines left-aligned at `NodePadding` from the left edge

```
┌──────────────────────┐
│    <<entity>>        │  ← annotation (centered)
│      Order           │  ← class name at label:centerY
├──────────────────────┤  ← divider at class:headerHeight
│ +id: Guid            │  ← left-aligned, compPad top/bottom
│ +status: string      │
├──────────────────────┤
│ +submit(): void      │
└──────────────────────┘
```

## Tests (`ClassDiagramLayoutTests.cs`, new)

19 focused layout/sizing tests using hand-built nodes (no parser dependency): width monotonicity, height growth with line/compartment count, annotation impact on sizing, `label:centerY` positioned inside header, no-overlap assertions for LR and TB layouts, and a regression guard confirming standard nodes are unchanged.

cases.head: f63a02462d1eebd5b06b45ebdf1d2705c919413a
cases.title: Add non-blocking partition access via PartitionGuard
cases.body:
### Summary
Introduces a PartitionGuard type to the partition-manager crate that provides both async (lock) and non-blocking (try_lock) access to partition storage, along with hardened arithmetic to prevent integer overflow.

## Motivation
When a task panics while holding a partition's mutex, the lock remains held. If the panic handler itself needs to access the same partition (e.g., to persist crash logs or diagnostic data), calling `lock().await` would deadlock. The handler is waiting on a lock that will never be released. By exposing `try_lock()`, callers like panic handlers can attempt non-blocking access and gracefully handle failure instead of deadlocking the system.

## Changes
- Added `PartitionGuard` struct with `lock()` (async) and `try_lock()` (non-blocking) constructors on Partition
- Implemented `BlockDevice`, `ReadNorFlash`, and `NorFlash` traits for PartitionGuard
- Re-exported `TryLockError` from embassy_sync for caller convenience
- Hardened all partition offset/size arithmetic with checked operations to prevent integer overflow
- Added unit tests covering guard-based read/write/erase, out-of-bounds access, overflow edge cases, and lock contention via `try_lock()`

cases.head: 6baec2abdca4d6b74b716ee677e88a03a1e63060
cases.title: Phase C PR 9 — optional board push from /clancy:approve-plan
cases.body:
## Summary

- Add **Step 4c — Optional board push (best-effort)** to `/clancy:approve-plan`. When approving a local plan-file stem in standalone+board mode, optionally push the approved plan to the source board ticket as a comment. Closes the "I have credentials and I want both modes" UX cliff.
- Two new flags on the command: `--push` (skip prompt + push immediately, also the retry path) and `--ticket KEY` (override Source auto-detect). Default interactive prompt is `[y/N]` with default No — never surprise-write to a board.
- Six per-platform comment-POST curl blocks duplicated from `plan.md` Step 5b under HTML-comment drift anchors. Workflow test byte-compares the two regions and fails on mismatch.
- 67 new tests (197 → 264 plan). Pre-push suite all green. Test counts elsewhere unchanged: 1608 core, 836 terminal, 51 brief.

## What ships

- **Step 4c run conditions** (slice 1): gates on Step 4a having written a marker AND board credentials being present in `.clancy/.env`. Either gate failing → silent skip + continue to Step 7. Step 4b's tail rewritten to route through 4c instead of jumping to Step 7.
- **Source read** (slice 2): reads `**Source:**` directly from `.clancy/plans/{stem}.md`. Single source of truth — does not chase the brief file the way Step 4b does.
- **Three-format parser** (slice 3): bracketed `[KEY] Title` is the only pushable format. Inline-quoted `"text"` and file-path `path/to.md` route to the skip branch with `BOARD_PUSH_SKIPPED_NO_TICKET`.
- **Per-platform key validation** (slice 4): six inline regexes (Jira `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\d+$`, GitHub `^#\d+$`, Linear `^[A-Z]+-\d+$`, Azure DevOps `^\d+$`, Shortcut `^\d+$`, Notion `^[0-9a-f]{32}$\|^[0-9a-f-]{36}$`). Single-board environment, no cross-board disambiguation. Mismatch → hard error with actionable message and exact retry command.
- **Decision matrix** (slice 5): six cells across `--push` × `--afk` × `--ticket`. Two-prompt non-`--afk` flow (Step 4 confirms approval, Step 4c confirms push) is intentional.
- **Drift anchors + byte-equality** (slices 0/6): canonical curl blocks live in `plan.md` Step 5b; an identical duplicate lives in `approve-plan.md` Step 4c between matching anchors. Editing one without updating the other fails the workflow test.
- **Push failure semantics** (slice 7): HTTP non-2xx logs the literal status; transport failure logs the lowercase error class (`network`/`timeout`/`dns`/`auth`). Marker stays, exact retry command printed, never exits non-zero.
- **EEXIST + `--push` retry path** (slice 8): re-running approve-plan with `--push` after a failed push falls through Step 4a's already-approved check, skips Step 4b (brief marker already updated), and re-attempts Step 4c. Original `sha256=` and `approved_at=` preserved. Without `--push`, EEXIST stops as today.
- **Notion flat-text note** (slice 9): conditional informational line in Step 7's local-mode success block when push target is Notion (only Notion — not the other five platforms), so users aren't surprised that markdown styling was flattened by Notion's `rich_text` model.
- **Command file flag docs** (slice 9): `commands/approve-plan.md` documents `--push` and `--ticket KEY` alongside the existing `--afk` from PR 7b.

## Locked spec decisions (recorded in `.claude/plans/plan-package-extraction.md` PR 9 section)

Six decisions locked before slice 0:

1. Push sub-step is **Step 4c**, not "Step 5a" (after 4b, before 7)
2. Retry semantics: **EEXIST + `--push` falls through to 4c** (no new flag, no marker deletion)
3. Source read from **`**Source:**` in the plan file** (not the brief)
4. Comment payload: **full plan content + one-line approval header**
5. Drift-prevention: **HTML comment anchors** (`<!-- curl-blocks:approve-plan-push:start/end -->`)
6. Progress.txt success row: **second row `LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN_PUSH | {stem} | {KEY}`** (not extended row)

## Reviews

**Architectural review** (self, after Plan + general-purpose agents both 529'd on Anthropic API capacity):
- COHESION: pass — pushing an approved plan as a board comment is the standalone+board UX cliff fix, symmetric with `/clancy:plan` Step 5b which already pushes plan content to board comments.
- LAYERING: pass — plan stays a leaf, zero new TS runtime deps, no `runPipeline` import, no core/terminal references. Markdown-only diff plus one TS test file in plan.
- SCOPE CREEP: none of substance — the 10 slices map directly onto the 6 locked decisions.

**DA review** (general-purpose agent on retry, after two prior 529s) caught 6 findings, all addressed in `fed52bd`:
- **H1** missing `LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN_PUSH` success row (the locked spec mandated it but slice 5 shipped without it) → added to Step 4c success branch
- **H2** stale Step 4a "After writing the marker" prose still said "jump to Step 7" (slice 1 only rewrote Step 4b) → rewrote to "continue to Step 4c"
- **M1** five new PR 9 tokens used `TOKEN | {stem} | {detail}` but the pre-existing `LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN` row (and `plan.md`'s `LOCAL_PLAN`/`LOCAL_REVISED`) use `{stem} | TOKEN | {detail}` → flipped all five for column-schema consistency
- **M2** the slice 8 EEXIST prose rendered the no-`--push` stop branch first as a full fenced block, with the retry branch buried after it → restructured so the retry branch comes first
- **L1** undocumented BOARD_PUSH_FAILED reason-field disambiguation contract → added explicit prefix-reservation note (HTTP statuses are numeric, error classes are a closed lowercase set, `key-mismatch:` prefix is reserved)
- **L2** slice 1's negative regex only scanned the 4b body slice — the same bug that hid H2 → widened to a regression test that scans the whole 4a→4c span

**Self-review**: 10 commits, clean gitmoji types, all scoped to `(plan)`. Final test count 264. Pre-push suite (`pnpm test && pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm format:check && pnpm knip && pnpm publint && pnpm attw`) all green.

## Test plan

- [x] CI runs the full pre-push quality suite on the merge commit
- [x] Smoke test (after merge): `/clancy:approve-plan {stem}` in standalone+board mode prompts `[y/N]` and respects default-No
- [x] Smoke test: `/clancy:approve-plan {stem} --push` skips the prompt and pushes
- [x] Smoke test: `/clancy:approve-plan {stem} --afk` (no `--push`) stays local-only and logs `LOCAL_ONLY`
- [x] Smoke test: `/clancy:approve-plan {stem} --push` after a simulated push failure falls through Step 4a's EEXIST gate and re-attempts the push
- [x] Smoke test: `/clancy:approve-plan {stem} --push --ticket WRONG-KEY` against a configured non-matching board produces the hard-error message and keeps the marker

cases.head: 5e9d78eba1ea7c359c17beae6351d22aaab1fb6b
cases.title: feat: complete Phase 43b — Kernel Trace Ring
cases.body:
## Summary

- Add per-core lockless `TraceRing<256>` in kernel-core with 8 host-side unit tests (empty, fill, wrap, 3x wrap, partial, event variants, for_each_chronological, copy_into)
- Define `TraceEvent` enum (`#[repr(C)]`) with 17 variants across scheduler (6), fork (4), and IPC (7) families
- Instrument 15 call sites across `scheduler.rs`, `process/mod.rs`, and `ipc/endpoint.rs`
- Wire `dump_trace_rings()` into panic handler and all fault handlers — prints per-core timeline via non-allocating `for_each_chronological()` (no heap allocation in crash path)
- Add `sys_ktrace` syscall (`0x1002`) with `ktrace()` wrapper in syscall-lib; uses stack buffer + `copy_into()` (no heap allocation)
- `TraceEntry` uses explicit `_pad: [u8; 7]` field (always zeroed) to prevent leaking uninit kernel memory via `repr(C)` padding
- `trace_ring` field in `PerCoreData` wrapped in `UnsafeCell` for sound interior mutability
- Feature-gate behind `trace` cargo feature (on by default, compiles out with `--no-default-features`)
- Add learning doc (`docs/43b-kernel-trace-ring.md`), roadmap design doc, and update task list to Complete

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p kernel-core` — 197 tests pass (including 8 trace ring tests)
- [x] `cargo xtask check` — clippy clean, formatting correct, host tests pass
- [x] `cargo xtask test` — all 8 QEMU integration tests pass
- [x] `cargo build -p kernel --no-default-features` — compiles without trace code
- [x] All docs conform to `docs/appendix/doc-templates.md` templates
